Item / Concern: Shot-by-shot production design audit to hit a cinematic standard
Notes: Benchmark question for every shot: 'Would I take this photo?' – currently 'almost no' across the test footage. Core insight: production design is the mechanism for adding meaning to pans and long takes – if the pan itself carries visual information throughout its duration (Tarkovsky's economy: every frame of a pan carries meaning, not just the first and last), the film can pack more meaning into less time, supporting runtime economy. Explicit thing to avoid: self-indulgent holding (holding a shot longer than necessary because the filmmaker likes it).
